headline: Record highs cool slightly as yields near multi-decade peak
body: The rally that carried the S&P 500 to its 28th record close of the year earlier this week lost some steam into midweek, with the S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Dow all pulling back from those highs -- the Dow's slip was the sharpest of the three, a pattern consistent with mega-cap tech and AI-linked names holding up better than the broader market. Futures firmed modestly afterward, suggesting the pullback is being read as a pause rather than a reversal so far. The bigger driver sits in the bond market: the 10-year Treasury yield has pushed up toward its highest levels in roughly two decades, and that move is doing more to set the day-to-day tone in equities than any single piece of company news, pressuring rate-sensitive and smaller-cap stocks more than the index heavyweights.

Underneath the headline levels, the conversation keeps circling back to concentration: a handful of AI and chip names continue to carry the indices, and recent earnings misses from large tech names have kept "AI bubble" framing in circulation among strategists, even as the broader uptrend itself hasn't broken. Attention is also turning toward the calendar -- bank earnings kick off the wider reporting season next week, and the Fed's late-October meeting is being priced mostly as a hold, which leaves data surprises as the main near-term catalyst. Retail and social-media sentiment didn't offer anything concrete enough to cite today -- a check of Reddit and Stocktwits chatter surfaced no clear, current read -- so this take leans more on price action, yields, and positioning commentary than on social buzz.
